answer: Interleaved Arrival Windows. Each identity must route its first N messages through a staggered, randomly permuted schedule whose completion latency is compared against the median of its declared cohort. A clone cluster that floods in parallel produces a tight burst that falls below the nadir of the expected spread and is throttled. Identities must then sustain spacing across a meadow of mixed traffic to stay eligible. The violet flag marks windows where variance collapses. Attackers pay by idling each clone through full windows, multiplying wall-clock cost per identity.
